title: QUIC RFC 9000 Initial Maximum Data Runtime Commit
purpose: Describe the bounded runtime path that treats the peer initial_max_data transport parameter as the initial connection-level send credit.
design_summary: Peer transport-parameter commit now applies initial_max_data directly to QuicConnectionStreamState.ConnectionSendLimit before stream send limits and stream-count limits are committed. Hosted client and server runtime construction starts with zero connection-level send credit because a local receive window is not peer-granted send credit; stream data becomes sendable only after the peer's transport parameters have supplied initial_max_data. MAX_DATA frames still use the existing monotonic increase path, while the transport-parameter commit path may replace a speculative test seed with the exact peer value.
data_and_state_considerations: ConnectionSendLimit remains the single connection-level send-credit source used by TryReserveSendCapacity. The peer initial_max_data path validates the QUIC variable-length integer boundary, writes the exact peer value, and keeps later send-capacity checks safe even if a stale speculative value had already exceeded the committed peer value.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A missing peer initial_max_data parameter commits zero initial connection-level send credit.
The peer transport-parameter value is applied exactly rather than merged with local receive-window configuration.
MAX_DATA frame handling remains monotonic and separate from the initial transport-parameter commit path.
Host runtimes start outbound connection-level send credit at zero until peer transport parameters are committed.
risks: This slice proves the initial connection-level data limit only; it does not claim max_udp_payload_size receiver processing, max_ack_delay alarm-delay policy, broader Section 18.2 closure, public flow-control APIs, 0-RTT remembered transport-parameter validation, or hosted interop readiness.
No new parser, serializer, encoder, or decoder is introduced. The existing transport-parameter codec proof remains separate, and this slice adds focused runtime commit proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S18P2-0008 by making the peer initial_max_data transport parameter authoritative for connection-level send credit on the committed runtime path.
